name: Productivity database
description: The OECD Productivity Database is the successor to the previous edition, offering improved coverage and detail. It consolidates and replaces earlier datasets, including those on productivity levels, productivity growth rates, and productivity by industry. The goal is to provide users with the most comprehensive, up-to-date, and granular productivity estimates available. Data are released on a rolling basis: each variable is published as soon as its underlying source is updated. The database includes annual labor productivity data -measured using both employment and hours worked - as well as detailed components of labor and capital inputs. In addition, quarterly estimates are available in a separate database covering productivity and unit labor costs.

source_notes: Regional rows such as OECD, EU27 and G7 are compiled from whichever member countries reported that particular figure in that particular year, so what they cover changes between one selection and the next. Two things follow. A breakdown can exceed the total it belongs to, because the two are built from different sets of countries. And a count for a region can come out far too small, because only some members reported it. Compare countries directly where the question allows it; read the regional rows as a rough centre of gravity rather than as a measurement of the region.
